podcast.title: Erratic Behavior and Asperger Syndrome (2001-2005)
podcast.body: Around 2001-2002, as The Vines gained traction in North America, Craig Nichols began exhibiting serious erratic behavior, including unusual habits like insisting on eating at McDonald's daily, and violent outbursts against journalists, audiences, and bandmates, which led to legal issues. He was officially diagnosed with Asperger's in 2005 and agreed to therapy. "We started hearing about some serious erratic behavior... In 2005, he was officially diagnosed in agreed to therapy."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Coping Mechanisms
podcast.body: Currently, Craig Nichols manages his Asperger's by rarely going out, avoiding 21st-century technology, and dedicating as much time as possible to his music. "Now he does his best by rarely going out, staying away from any 21st century technology, spending as much time as he possibly can to his music."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Post-Diagnosis Deterioration and Arrest
podcast.body: Despite initial therapy after his 2005 Asperger's diagnosis, Craig Nichols' condition deteriorated, leading to his arrest for assaulting his parents. "That worked for a while, but then he deteriorated again and was arrested for assaulting his parents."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Australian Origins and McDonald's Meeting
xref.body: The Vines were formed in Sydney, Australia, in 1994. Singer and guitarist Craig Nichols and bass player Patrick Matthews met while working together at their local McDonald's. "They were formed in Sydney, Australia in 1994, when singer and guitarist Craig Nichols and bass player Patrick Matthews met while working at their local McDonald's."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Eccentric Frontman Craig Nichols
xref.body: Lead singer Craig Nichols was described as an eccentric frontman whose erratic behavior became part of the band's story. He reportedly smoked a lot of dope, insisted on eating at McDonald's at least once a day, and was volatile both in interviews and on stage. His behavior was later explained by a diagnosis of Asperger syndrome, a form of autism. "Their story was the help of the fact that they had an eccentric frontman in the form of Craig Nichols."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Nirvana Influence
xref.body: Both Craig Nichols and Patrick Matthews were huge fans of Nirvana, specifically drawing inspiration from the parts of Nirvana's catalog where Kurt Cobain stripped everything down to the basics. This foundational influence shaped The Vines' own musical approach. "Both were huge fans of Nirvana and wanted to do something like that. Specifically, the parts of the Nirvana canon were Kurt stripped everything down to the basics."
